PC: The learner asks about the standardized historian’s relationship to the patient during the interview.
The learner asks if the standardized historian is the primary caregiver. If completed, the learner asks if the custody arrangement is formal or informal.
The learner asks why the patient is in the standardized historian’s custody.
The learner asks about the standardized historian’s medical history as well as the patient’s.
The learner asks about what medications are in the home. If completed, the learner asks where the medications are stored.
The learner inquires about patient’s current asthma medications and dosages.
The learner provides guidance regarding how to properly administer the patient’s medications.
The learner discusses possible asthma triggers.
MK: The learner establishes that the standardized historian is not correctly administering the patient’s medications.
ICS: The learner turns off the T.V. before beginning to gather the history.
The learner introduces him/herself to the standardized historian.
The learner maintains eye contact with the standardized historian while gathering the history.
The learner sits at the same level as the standardized historian to gather the history.
The learner speaks in a slow, clear voice
